newsitem.title: UK: High grade cobalt drifts as Gecamines to reopen.
newsitem.headline: High grade cobalt drifts as Gecamines to reopen.

text.p: News that Zaire's cobalt and copper producer Gecamines will reopen its head offices in Lubumbashi and resume normal business on Monday saw recent upside sentiment slacken in the cobalt market on Friday.
In European trading high grade material was last around $24 a pound, down around $1 from levels seen earlier this week.
"It was largely expected that the reopening of Gecamines was likely to cap the current rally," one London trader commented.

Gecamines, Zaire's state owned mining company, closed its Lubumbashi headquarters situated in the mineral rich Shaba region on Monday as rebel forces of Laurent Kabila advanced on Zaire's second city.

Several traders had expected the facility to be closed for around a month, though most traders polled by Reuters recently said the mines would not be closed for long as cobalt and copper are hard currency earners for the central African state.
Traders and analyst of the cobalt market will monitor the developments in Zaire closely as the region has huge mineral deposits.
Under President Mobutu Zaire's mining operations lacked capital investment which has seen output in both cobalt and copper drop dramatically.

In the early 1980s cobalt production was around 15,000 tonnes a year, versus current levels of around 5,000 tonnes -- still near a fifth of global production. Output of copper has tumbled from around 500,000 tonnes to near 40,000 over the same period.

A feasibility study on the giant Tenke Fungurume copper/cobalt deposit in Zaire is expected to be completed by the end of 1997, Brian Spratley, Technical director of Mining Development Services Ltd (MDS) said on Thursday.
MDS is a subsidiary company of Canada's Tenke Mining Corp, who are developing a vast mine in the mineral-rich Shaba province after signing a deal with Zaire's government last December.
The project, the first major foreign investment in Zaire since the 1970s, is a joint-venture with state-owned Gecamines who have a 45 percent holding.
Mineral reserves at the deposit are estimated at 93 million tonnes, grading at 4.59 percent copper and 0.37 percent cobalt.
Tenke's intention is to start up copper production by mid-2000 at an initial rate of 100,000 tonnes a year, working up to 400,000 tonnes annually.
Cobalt production will be 8,000 tonnes, or some 25 percent of the current world market.
